subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical all-configured-model health check, or should that behavior be folded into fallback-chain or staged model-migration UX first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent command surface makes real provider calls and overlaps two other open model-safety requests, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Approve Status Probe Extension
options.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status` with conservative defaults, docs, focused tests, and redacted live CLI proof while leaving fallback-chain and migration workflows separate.

options.title: Unify Model-Safety UX First
options.body: Design one model-safety workflow that covers all-configured-model probes, fallback-chain tests, and staged promotion before adding another CLI flag.

options.title: Defer Core CLI
options.body: Keep current auth/profile probes and rely on external monitoring or manual provider checks until maintainers want a broader core diagnostic surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Status Probe Extension
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status` with conservative defaults, docs, focused tests, and redacted live CLI proof while leaving fallback-chain and migration workflows separate.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history in model status/probe and provider-routing work and has already been the clearest product-review voice for adjacent model diagnostics.
